skills.name: Scaffold monorepo folder structure
skills.capability: Initializes the Pulseboard repository root with a workspace layout separating the client (dashboard + status-page surfaces) and server (shared API) packages.
skills.prompt_template: You are setting up the root of the Pulseboard monorepo. Create a root package.json with npm workspaces pointing at client and server packages, and create the top-level directory structure: client/src/dashboard, client/src/status-page, client/src/shared, and server/src. Do not add product feature code — only the scaffolding needed for later epics to build on.
acceptance_criteria: Root package.json declares workspaces including client and server
client/src contains dashboard, status-page, and shared subdirectories
server/src directory exists for the Express API

skills.name: Initialize React 18 + Vite frontend

testcases.name: client declares react and react-dom deps

skills.capability: Scaffolds the client package with Vite and React 18, wiring an entry point capable of mounting the dashboard and status-page surfaces.
skills.prompt_template: You are bootstrapping the Pulseboard frontend using Vite with the React 18 template inside the client/ workspace package. Add react and react-dom as dependencies pinned to v18, configure vite.config.js, and create a minimal entry point (main.jsx/App.jsx) that will later route between the dashboard and status-page surfaces. Keep it minimal — no product UI yet.
acceptance_criteria: client/package.json lists react and react-dom as dependencies
client/package.json lists vite as a devDependency
client/vite.config.js exists and configures the React plugin
npm run dev in client starts the Vite dev server without error

skills.name: Initialize Express backend
skills.capability: Scaffolds the server package with Node.js and Express, exposing a base app instance ready for API routes and a local SQLite/JSON store.
skills.prompt_template: You are bootstrapping the Pulseboard backend inside the server/ workspace package using Node.js and Express. Add express as a dependency, create server/src/app.js exporting a configured Express app, and server/src/index.js that starts it on a configurable port. No incident/status-page routes yet — only the base server scaffold and a health endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: server/package.json lists express as a dependency
server/src/app.js exports an Express application instance
Running the server starts without error and listens on a port

skills.name: Configure Vitest test framework
skills.capability: Sets up Vitest as the shared test runner for both client and server packages, including jsdom environment for React component tests.
skills.prompt_template: You are configuring Vitest as the single test framework for the Pulseboard monorepo, covering both the client (React, jsdom environment) and server (Node environment) packages. Add vitest as a devDependency at the appropriate workspace levels, create vitest.config.js for each package, and add a `test` script to each package.json plus a root aggregate script. Do not write product tests yet, only the runner configuration.
acceptance_criteria: client/package.json and server/package.json declare vitest as a devDependency
client/vitest.config.js sets the test environment to jsdom
Root package.json defines a test script that runs vitest across workspaces
npm test exits 0 on a fresh checkout with no test files failing

skills.name: Create .adlc.json project config
skills.capability: Authors the .adlc.json configuration file declaring the test command, tech stack, and required services for downstream agent tooling.
skills.prompt_template: You are authoring the .adlc.json configuration file at the repo root for Pulseboard. Set test_command to the command that runs the full Vitest suite, declare tech_stack as node and react, and set required_services to an empty array since the app uses a local SQLite/JSON store with no external services. This file drives how downstream automation runs and validates the project.
acceptance_criteria: .adlc.json declares a test_command referencing the test runner
.adlc.json declares tech_stack including node and react
.adlc.json declares required_services as an empty array

skills.name: Configure ESLint and Prettier baseline

testcases.name: root declares eslint and prettier devDependencies

skills.capability: Establishes a shared ESLint and Prettier configuration across client and server packages to enforce consistent code style.
skills.prompt_template: You are setting up a shared ESLint and Prettier baseline for the Pulseboard monorepo. Add eslint and prettier as devDependencies, create root-level .eslintrc (or eslint.config.js) and .prettierrc configs covering both React (client) and Node (server) code, and add lint/format scripts to package.json. Do not fix unrelated existing lint violations outside this scaffolding task.
acceptance_criteria: Root package.json declares eslint and prettier as devDependencies
A root ESLint config file exists and covers client and server source
A .prettierrc config file exists at the repo root
npm run lint exits 0 on the freshly scaffolded codebase

skills.name: Configure Tailwind CSS baseline
skills.capability: Installs and configures Tailwind CSS in the client package so both the dashboard (dark theme) and status-page (light theme) surfaces can use utility classes and design tokens.
skills.prompt_template: You are configuring Tailwind CSS as the styling baseline for the Pulseboard client package. Add tailwindcss, postcss, and autoprefixer as devDependencies, generate tailwind.config.js and postcss.config.js scoped to client/src, and create the base CSS file with @tailwind directives imported by the app entry point. Leave theme customization (dark/light tokens, severity colors) minimal — just the working baseline.
acceptance_criteria: client/package.json declares tailwindcss, postcss, and autoprefixer as devDependencies
client/tailwind.config.js exists with a content path covering client/src
client/src has a base stylesheet containing the @tailwind directives
The client build succeeds with Tailwind classes applied

skills.name: Add CI smoke tests for build health
skills.capability: Adds a minimal end-to-end smoke test suite covering an API health check endpoint and a trivial React component render to confirm the environment builds and runs.
skills.prompt_template: You are adding minimal smoke tests that prove the Pulseboard environment is wired correctly end-to-end. Add a GET /health endpoint on the Express app returning a 200 status with a simple JSON body, and write one server-side test asserting that response using Supertest. Add one trivial React component and a client-side test asserting it renders using React Testing Library. These are scaffolding smoke tests, not product feature tests.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health on the Express app returns HTTP 200 with a status field
A server-side smoke test exercises the /health endpoint via Supertest and passes
A client-side smoke test renders a trivial component and passes
The full test suite (npm test) passes in CI on a clean checkout

skills.name: Add Vercel-deployable build config
skills.capability: Adds Vercel deployment configuration so the client build and Express API can both be deployed from the same repository.
skills.prompt_template: You are adding Vercel deployment configuration for Pulseboard. Create a vercel.json at the repo root that builds the client package as a static site and exposes the server package's Express app as a serverless function/API route, and ensure the client's build script outputs to the directory Vercel expects. Verify the configuration by running a local Vercel build (vercel build) and confirming it completes without error.
acceptance_criteria: vercel.json exists at the repo root and defines builds for both client and server
client/package.json defines a build script producing a static output directory
A local Vercel build completes successfully with no configuration errors
